tickets.title: Cross-tab refresh-token mutex (single-use rotation double-spend)
tickets.summary: Found 2026-07-13 via api access log during the T-154.1 pause: two editor tabs share the single-use refresh token; tab A rotates it, tab B later POSTs the stale one -> /auth/refresh 401 -> the whole browser session dies (log: 12:13 local, registry+compat 401 -> refresh 401 -> all subsequent 401). The single-flight helper (apps/website/frontend/src/api/refresh.ts) serializes refreshes WITHIN a tab only. Fix: cross-tab mutex around refresh (Web Locks API, BroadcastChannel fallback) + adopt the rotated pair from the winning tab (storage event), so N tabs spend one rotation. Repro: open the editor in two tabs, wait out the access TTL, act in the stale tab.

tickets.title: Session-expired UX - 401s must not masquerade as empty data
tickets.summary: Sibling of T-155 (same 2026-07-13 incident): when auth dies, GET /registry and GET /factions fail and the UI silently degrades - the Arsenal shows the non-character guard ("Loadout applies to placed characters") because the catalog is empty, and the Factions palette shows the "No factions yet" author-CTA. Operator read it as data loss. Fix: distinguish query-error (esp. 401 after failed refresh) from genuinely-empty responses; surface one clear "session expired - log in again" banner/toast with a dev-login shortcut in dev, and make useRegistry/useFactionLibrary consumers render an error state, never the empty-state copy, on failure.

tickets.title: TBD Framework — Arma-3-parity event mod (factory + spine)
tickets.summary: Rebuild the Arma 3 mission workflow inside Reforger: website Mission Creator = Eden, compiled mission JSON = the .pbo, and the mod supplies everything Reforger does NOT ship (lobby, briefing, slotting, spawn, spectator, admin). Stage 1 FACTORY shipped: host-aware execution, a 1.3s headless Enfusion compile gate on the native dedicated server (no Workbench), a mechanical CRF symbol index (266 files / 71,606 LOC), and a capability matrix whose UNTRIAGED gate turns a forgotten capability into a build error. Stage 2 is the TBD-owned event spine (ONE LIFE + admin respawn; macOS-methodology UI on Aegis tokens). CRF is an Arma-Public-License ORACLE — indexed, never vendored. ABSORBS T-068.13. BLOCKED: the only remaining slice is T-181.16 (executor: human) — a live two-client E2E on a dedicated server. Not agent-actionable; moved off `ready` on 2026-07-26 so the fleet does not pick it up.

T-181.0.notes: scripts/lib/hostrun.sh — agent shell is a debian:12 container; builds/game binaries route to the host. CORRECTED an earlier misdiagnosis that xtask was glibc-broken; it never was.

T-181.1.notes: scripts/mod/compile.sh + make mod-compile/-selftest. Native ArmaReforgerServer; no Workbench/Proton/GPU. Measured 780ms compile, 1.3s gate (was 90-120s + a human click).

T-181.2.notes: enf bin in tools/tbd-tools; 266 files / 71,606 LOC / 3,359 symbols / 119 RplProps / 78 modded overrides -> .ai/artifacts/enf-index/crf_*.tsv.

T-181.2.1.notes: docs/mod/capability_verdicts.tsv + make verify-capability. 57 capabilities, zero untriaged. A forgotten CRF capability is now a build error.

T-181.3.notes: enf carve + index vanilla + make enf-carve. PARTIAL BY NATURE: only a subset of vanilla script ships uncompressed. Got 610 files / 41,958 LOC / 1,106 declarations (882 SCR_*) — AI/behaviour-tree, camera, actions, UI components, WB plugins. SCR_BaseGameMode / SCR_PossessSpawnData / SCR_PossessSpawnRequestComponent / SCR_RespawnSystemComponent / ChimeraMenuBase are ABSENT as plaintext (compressed) — recorded as known-missing in docs/mod/vanilla_carve_coverage.md, not faked. Output gitignored (BI copyright); only the derived index is committed. Follow-up: inflate compressed pak blocks via PakVfs and re-carve.

T-181.3.1.notes: Official BI Script API mirror + parser (enf apidoc, scripts/mod/fetch-vanilla-api.sh, make enf-apidoc). 7,990 classes indexed. CLOSES the T-181.3 gap: SCR_BaseGameMode/PossessSpawnData/PossessSpawnRequestComponent/RespawnSystemComponent/ChimeraMenuBase all resolve with full member lists incl. `static SCR_PossessSpawnData FromEntity(notnull IEntity)`. Signatures only, no bodies — CRF stays the behavioural oracle. Operator's suggestion that the data exists online was correct.

T-181.3.2.notes: enf extract — pulls vanilla scripts BY REAL PATH from the pak FILE table (operator asked 'what about the MCP?' — the MCP's game_browse DOES list them; its game_read fails). Fixed PakVfs to fall back zlib->raw deflate. Result: 2,483/6,495 scripts extracted (all the UNCOMPRESSED ones); combined vanilla index now 2,099 files / 72,226 LOC / 1,659 declarations. BARRIER: the 4,012 compressed entries use a codec that is neither zlib nor deflate, with no method flag (all-zero method bytes). enfusion-mcp only calls inflateSync so it cannot read them either — that error is why vanilla source looked unavailable. Follow-up T-181.3.3: identify the codec (LZ4 block is the hypothesis) to unlock the gameplay layer.

T-181.3.3.notes: SOLVED — but not by cracking the codec. Operator found arexplorer.zeroy.com: a Doxygen build of the SAME game version (1.7.0.54) with SOURCE_BROWSER on, 6,495 *_source.html pages exactly matching the pak script count, each with FULL METHOD BODIES. Built scripts/mod/fetch-vanilla-source.sh (curated by default, cached, rate-limited — it is one person's site) + `enf source` (Doxygen page -> real .c, incl. name demangling _s_c_r___base_game_mode_8c -> SCR_BaseGameMode.c). Vanilla index now 2,116 files / 88,670 LOC / 1,702 decls. SCR_BaseGameMode, SCR_RespawnSystemComponent, ChimeraMenuBase, SCR_SpawnRequestComponent all resolve to real source. The pak-codec RE is now MOOT — negative results retained in docs/mod/vanilla_carve_coverage.md only so nobody repeats them.

T-181.4.notes: docs/mod/TBD_MOD_DESIGN.md (north star) + enf citations + make verify-oracle + make verify-no-crf-leak. 14 @idx citations resolve; injecting the hallucinated 'RequestSlotChange' makes it exit 1. Leak gate allows CRF_ in comments (attribution) and treats vanilla GUIDs as engine facts — both false-positive classes measured and handled.

T-181.5.notes: DEPRIORITISED: make mod-compile (native, 1.3s) removed most of the reason to open Workbench at all. Only world/prefab authoring and PIE visual checks still need it. Do this when a slice actually requires the editor.

T-181.6.notes: claude-code slices only; verify must exit 0 incl. mod-compile; never auto-ship; Workbench lockfile.

T-181.7.notes: UI framework @ fb36da81. TBD_MenuStack/TBD_MenuBase/TBD_ShellScreen/TBD_ListBox + TBD_UITheme (Aegis tokens) + 2 .layout + chimeraMenus.conf. Listbox POOLS and re-binds rows (vanilla SCR_ListBoxComponent creates/destroys per item — wrong for 128 slots). BLOCKER: chimeraMenus.conf is invisible to the engine until Workbench regenerates resourceDatabase.rdb — 'GUI (E): Menu preset TBD_UIShell not found!'. Proven by elimination across 4 path/meta variants; no script escape hatch (RegisterPreset/OpenMenuByLayout do not exist). Needs one slow-lane Workbench pass. COMPILE-VERIFIED ONLY — no visual claim.

T-181.8.notes: MOSTLY ALREADY BUILT — the factory caught this before a rewrite. TBD_FrameworkManager already has enum TBD_EGameStage{LOADING,LOBBY,BRIEFING,SAFE_START,LIVE,END,DEBRIEF}, a replicated [RplProp(onRplName:"OnStageReplicated")] m_Stage, SetStage()+Replication.BumpMe(), and IsFrameworkWorld(). Remaining gap is stage CONTENT: BRIEFING and SAFE_START are enum-only (no logic).

T-181.8.1.notes: SUPERSEDED — triaged 2026-07-25 and closed without its own implementation, because later slices built everything it named. Its whole note was 'Slotting depends on it.' with no title anywhere (it was never in wave_plan.tsv), so the scope had to be recovered from its parent T-181.8: 'Remaining gap is stage CONTENT: BRIEFING and SAFE_START are enum-only (no logic).' Both are now closed, verified in TBD_FrameworkManager: OnEnterLobby/OnEnterBriefing/OnEnterLive exist as real entry handlers; BRIEFING carries content (:778, :811) via T-181.23 (payload), T-181.27 (ORDERS), T-181.28 (JIP catch-up) and T-181.38 (flow.briefingSeconds); SAFE_START is owned by TBD_SafestartManager (T-181.17, hardened by T-181.33) and SetStage refuses the transition outright when that manager is absent (:732). The stated dependency — slotting — shipped in T-181.9.x. Kept as a shipped row rather than deleted so the supersession is visible to anyone who finds the reference.

T-181.9.notes: Slotting authority completed. ClaimSlot already existed (PS-shaped first-come guard). Added: ReleaseSlot (lobby-only change-of-mind; refused once deployed), BuildSlotRoster (per-slot key/faction/group/role/state/holder as TSV — the data T-181.9.1's picker binds to, deliberately plain text so authority is testable from the server log before any widget exists; state = OPEN|HELD|DEAD), and a ONE-LIFE INTEGRITY FIX: ClaimSlot and ReleaseSlot now both refuse a dead player. Without it a dead player could release their slot and claim a fresh one, bypassing one life entirely. Landmine caught by the compile gate in 1.3s: `out` is a RESERVED KEYWORD in Enfusion (out-param modifier) and cannot be a variable name.

T-181.9.1.notes: Lobby slot picker @ 56ad6d16. SUPERSEDES T-068.13. Server-fed roster parsed from BuildSlotRoster() and nothing else, so it cannot disagree with the authority. Optimistic claim held as a pending intent keyed on the slot until the authority rules on THAT seat — without it a refresh in flight makes the seat flicker away and back, which reads exactly like losing it. Refusal names the actual winner off the authority's own roster. Deploy is deliberately NOT optimistic. Back button hidden (the stack is empty beneath LOBBY, so 'back' is a trap). Deliberately does NOT filter the other side — you cannot pick a side you cannot see; side discipline starts at the briefing. m_bAutoDeploy REPORTED not flipped: the wave is currently the only working way into the world.

T-181.9.2.notes: Briefing screen @ d42eb681. Side discipline enforced AT THE WIRE: clients hold no mission document at all, the enemy ORBAT is never serialised, delivery is RplRcver.Owner, and the request carries no faction so a modified client cannot ask for the other side. ORBAT derived from slots[] not orbat{} because the latter models only roles/count, dropping callsign/slot/kit. GAP: `briefings` prose is unparsed — the screen shows structure without orders (T-181.23).

T-181.10.notes: JSON loadouts @ 4b1ff732. optic+magazine were parsed and DISCARDED — now mounted into weapon storage. Honest per-field failure lines naming slot+item; nakedness guard. Closed a real hole: body reuse now keyed on IDENTITY, so a player taking a vacated slot cannot inherit the previous occupant's fired mags/damage, while a mid-life reconnect still gets its own body. AdminRespawn forces a fresh body. IsBodyDead treated a missing CharacterControllerComponent as ALIVE (bug). COMPILE-VERIFIED ONLY — magazine chambering and optic mounting need eyes.

T-181.11.notes: ONE LIFE in TBD_SpawnManager: m_bOneLife attribute (default on), m_mDeadPlayers map, OnPlayerKilled now terminal — slot STAYS claimed so the seat is not recycled and reconnect still resolves. Added IsPlayerDead() and CountAliveForFaction() (the primitive T-181.13 side-eliminated needs; counts claimed slots so a never-deployed player cannot silently end the round). m_bAutoDeploy path retained for PIE.

T-181.11.1.notes: AdminRespawn(playerId, byAdmin) — server-authority only, refuses non-dead and disconnected players, re-materializes a dressed body on the player's own slot, writes an audit line, and re-marks dead on FAILED rather than leaving limbo. Chat: `#tbd respawn <playerId>` and `#tbd dead`. Permission reuses vanilla SCR_PlayerListedAdminManagerComponent.IsPlayerOnAdminList (so T-181.11.1 permissions were already HAVE).

T-181.11.2.notes: Admin menu @ c4708f72. A FRONT-END onto the same server authority as the chat commands, not a second implementation — TBD_AdminService is the single choke point and permission is checked at four entry points including the READ gate, so a non-admin's snapshot contains a refusal string and nothing else (no roster to render even with a patched client). Deploy and Respawn deliberately kept separate: AdminRespawn refuses anyone not dead and DeployPlayerEx refuses anyone who is, so one button would silently no-op half the time. Force-stage is armed-then-confirmed. Audit ring is capped at 60 with repeat refusals console-only, so a client spamming refusals cannot flush real actions out of an admin's view. Avoided a 4th modded SCR_PlayerController by extending the existing block. PERMISSION IS PROVEN BY CONSTRUCTION, NOT BY A LIVE NON-ADMIN ATTEMPT — needs the operator.

T-181.12.notes: Spectator @ 3845765e. Camera REIMPLEMENTED not derived, justified: SCR_ManualCamera's behaviour lives in a prefab (same rdb blocker for nothing), it is the editor camera, and it cannot follow. Reuses vanilla's ManualCameraContext actions so FREE FLIGHT WORKS BEFORE ANY WORKBENCH PASS. Faction-restricted by default: under one life half the server ends up spectating while still in squad voice, so unrestricted is a live intel feed, not a viewer. Client-side poll for enter/exit because 'am I spectating' is a client question — also covers reconnect-on-spent-life, which no death hook sees. HOOK NEEDED: spectator host entity for streaming (see T-181.24).

T-181.13.notes: JSON-driven round end. TBD_MissionWinConditionsStruct {mode, endOn[]} added to the mission document (@contract mission.schema.json#/$defs/winConditions) + TBD_MissionLoader.HasEndTrigger(). TickWinConditions in TBD_FrameworkManager (2s, armed only on LIVE and only if the mission declared faction_eliminated). Guards: ignores factions with 0 claimed slots (unfielded != eliminated), requires >=2 contesting factions (a solo test cannot end the round), unregisters itself off LIVE. time_limit and the other three enum triggers parse but are not evaluated yet — declared, not silently dropped.

T-181.13.1.notes: Results POST + the validator MAJOR. Validator warnings across the four goldens 28 -> 3 (bridgehead 18->0, empty-warning-fields 7->2, slot-loadout-coverage 2->0, montfort 1->1 unrelated); baseline tightened. CORRECTED A LANDMINE THE COMMAND CENTER WROTE: an instrumented boot dumping per-slot null/count state showed `ref array<>` is NOT over-allocated when the key is absent — cargo came back non-null on exactly the slots authoring a cargo key and null on those that did not, BOTH POLARITIES IN ONE RUN — while `ref <class>` is allocated regardless. The doc had said the distinction did not matter and not to spend a run on it; it matters, and the agent got it free from a run it had to do anyway. That fact is load-bearing: gear presence is genuinely unobservable (absent gear and gear:{} both parse to ten empty strings) but cargo presence is PROOF the block was authored, which is what finally makes the 'neither gear nor cargo' branch reachable. Results: no new endpoint, no Rust change; omits unmeasured stats rather than sending zeros, because absent says 'not measured' where 0 claims 'measured, and none'. outcome=success only when faction_eliminated was declared AND the arithmetic resolved. LIVE END-TO-END POST PROVED against a capture endpoint mirroring telemetry.rs: two real requests from 'Arma Reforger/1.7.0.54 (Headless; LINUX)', all 9 and 15 contract checks passed, hostile role label escaped correctly. Measured: the engine sends the body Transfer-Encoding: CHUNKED, so a receiver reading Content-Length sees an empty body. Shared accessor for T-181.35 is TBD_PlayerIdentity.GetArmaId — it deliberately returns EMPTY rather than a player:<id> lease, and such players are dropped, because users.arma_id is UNIQUE and empty ids would collapse rows and bind one account to everybody. ATTENDANCE INERT until T-181.35; LogIdentityCensus prints the no-op every round.

T-181.14.notes: Mission validation @ 915b78a8. TBD_MissionValidator (27 checks, all run in one pass, ERROR vs WARNING) + TBD_Log. Rejected mission holds the server in LOADING via the existing IsValid gate — no FrameworkManager edit. '#tbd validate' replays findings in game; every #tbd reply leads with a failure banner. Decision table verified offline against both golden missions + 14 mutations (proves the table, NOT the Enfusion runtime). Needs a hook: TBD_Log.Stage(prev,next) has no caller.

T-181.15.notes: JIP / reconnect hardened. Requirement 1 was ALREADY implemented — this made it survivable. THE REAL HAZARD WAS THE CALLQUEUE, which no prior audit had touched: five deferred callbacks carried a raw playerId across disconnect, and ScriptCallQueue.Remove cancels by FUNCTION so one player's timer cannot be cancelled alone. Worst case measured: RedeployAfterDeath would DEPLOY a fresh joiner into a dead player's slot. Closed with a lazily-opened connection epoch (lazy because vanilla only self-audits Listen && playerId>1, so a listen host's player 1 may never hit the join hook and stamping 0 would make its retry ladder permanently inert). Every int-keyed per-player map was audited and found SAFE — all erased on disconnect. The player:<id> residual was WORSE than recorded: it leaked the seat AND the life, so a recycled id arrived DEAD. Closed by splitting IsIdentityKey (backend or synthesized) from IsDurableKey (backend only) — having only one predicate is what caused it. JIP DECISION: deploy at any stage LOBBY..LIVE, because a player who crashed before deploying is INDISTINGUISHABLE at the join hook from a walk-up latecomer, so a 'too late' rule cannot be written that does not also strand the crash. One-life guard still protects the invariant. OPERATOR CAVEAT: in keyMode=NUMERIC a reconnector gets a SECOND seat, so CountClaimedForFaction over-counts — another reason a dedicated server with real identities is required for an event. COMPILE-VERIFIED ONLY: every behavioural claim needs a dedicated server + 2 clients; PIE cannot exercise any of it. Also unanswerable from this lane: whether SCR_ReconnectComponent is on GameMode_Plain.et (a prefab question) — the code is correct either way.

T-181.16.notes: Dedicated server + 2 real clients, full loop.

T-181.17.notes: Safestart / warmup phase. Damage suppressed via EnableDamageHandling(false) with VERIFIED restoration and a watchdog, so a failed restore cannot leave an event permanently invulnerable. Admin surface: '#tbd safestart [status|go|<seconds>]' answers 'is damage actually off right now' in one command. THE MOST VALUABLE THING THIS SLICE PRODUCED WAS A HOLE, NOT A FEATURE: the agent reported that it could not verify its component instantiates, because -scenarioId alone does not load the world on the headless server. Chasing that found the real cause — -config and -addons are MUTUALLY EXCLUSIVE, and -addons+-scenarioId with no -config prints 'Game successfully created' and then idles without ever hosting. Three slices had by then added components to TBD_GameMode.et with NOTHING proving any of them instantiates. Closed by T-181.17.1.

T-181.17.1.notes: World-boot gate. Closes the hole T-181.17 surfaced: nothing proved the components on TBD_GameMode.et instantiate, and the compile gate is blind to prefab wiring. Two engine landmines found and recorded — -config and -addons are MUTUALLY EXCLUSIVE (hard fatal), and -addons+-scenarioId with no -config prints 'Game successfully created' then idles without ever hosting, which is why the earlier harness 'proved' nothing. Working recipe: -addonsDir + -config with the addon in game.mods[] keyed by the addon.gproj GUID. Added TBD_FrameworkManager.PrintComponentRollCall() + scripts/mod/world-boot.sh, wired into wave.sh gate. ALL FIVE COMPONENTS VERIFIED PRESENT. HARDENED AFTER THE WAVE-4 VERIFIER BROKE IT: the roll-call alone passed a prefab containing TBD_ThisComponentDoesNotExist (it only checks names it was told about), so the gate now also greps the engine's own name-independent 'WORLD (E): Unknown class'; error attribution was classifying by MESSAGE TEXT and let six genuine TBD failures through (one differing only in the case of Scripts/Game/), so triage is now fail-closed with an explicit vanilla allowlist; Print(localVar) emits the DECLARATION not the value, so the selftest fixtures had never matched reality; added OnDelete to cancel four callqueue entries that survived an in-process scenario restart; ports randomised off the dev config so the gate no longer collides with the operator's server or a parallel run (proven with two concurrent boots). Selftest now pins 10 cases. NOT runtime evidence: the boot has no backend, so the stage machine never leaves LOADING.

T-181.18.notes: AO / play-area poly-zones + out-of-bounds. Polygon parsing added (ref array<ref array<float>>) — polygon zones previously parsed to nothing. TBD_ZoneGeometry (circle + crossing-number polygon), TBD_Zone, TBD_ZoneRegistry, TBD_PlayAreaComponent (1 Hz server tick, warn -> grace -> penalty). Terminal penalty implemented in full but OFF by default (rules.penalty defaults to 'warn'); a kill routes through SCR_CharacterDamageManagerComponent.Kill so it lands in the existing OnPlayerKilled -> MarkLifeSpent path — no second death path, TBD_SpawnManager untouched. OPERATOR-VISIBLE: golden-missions/bridgehead-at-levie.json zone z4 already authors penalty=kill graceSeconds=30, so the REFERENCE MISSION will permanently remove a player 30 s after they leave the AO. Geometry proven with 25 runtime cases via a shadow addon incl. concave notch, both winding orders, rays through vertices — with a deliberately-wrong expectation confirming the harness can print FAIL. FOUND A MAJOR LANDMINE: JsonLoadContext allocates nested ref struct fields even when the JSON key is ABSENT, so a null check is not a presence test. Also fixed a latent dead guard in GetSpawnZoneForFaction that would have returned map-corner (0,0) for a polygon spawn zone. NOT runtime-verified: no player ever joins under world-boot, so no enforcement path has run against a real player.

T-181.19.notes: Map markers from mission JSON. Consumer only — T-181.23 already parsed them and nothing read them. Rides Reforger's own SCR_MapMarkerManagerComponent.InsertStaticMarker with PLACED_CUSTOM, matching vanilla SCR_BaseTutorialStage.CreateMarkerCustom and CRF's own usage, so NO new .conf/.layout and the rdb blocker does not apply. PER-FACTION ENFORCEMENT IS STRUCTURAL: the request RPC takes NO ARGUMENTS, so a client cannot phrase the question; the side is read server-side from the assigned slot; reply is RplRcver.Owner; client insert is isLocal so received markers cannot re-enter replication. No slot = served=false, zero rows (fail closed). Discovered the icon enum vocabulary BY COMPILATION (23 members) rather than guessing, and resolves against the engine's own 91 placed icons first so all 91 are authorable with no maintenance. Corrected the command center's brief: 'all four fields required so a marker is complete' is true of PRESENCE, false of CONTENT — icon/label have no minLength and empty-warning-fields.json ships a marker with both empty. NOT runtime-observed: nothing visual, no client ever joined. Adds a 5th modded class SCR_PlayerController (overrides no vanilla method, adds no menu preset enum). || POST-MERGE (wave-5 verifier, MINOR, not yet fixed): a slot CHANGE leaves the previous side's markers on the client's map. TBD_SpawnManager.ReleaseSlot refuses only a spent life or an already-deployed player, so a live un-deployed player can release a BLUFOR slot and claim an OPFOR one; the client is already s_bServed and TBD_MarkerClient.Tick has cancelled itself, so nothing re-requests and the served->unserved clear path in Accept() is unreachable. Recovery is the next map open, but OnMapOpen returns before Request() inside MAP_REQUEST_MIN_GAP_MS (3 s) and stale markers are drawn on open and only replaced a round trip later. THE SERVER SIDE IS SOUND — the verifier could not phrase a cross-side request; this is purely a stale client cache.

T-181.20.notes: Golden fixtures @ bae5d1d1. slot-loadout-coverage.json is the FIRST golden to carry a slot loadout block (all 10 gear refs, cargo at the schema minimum, the primary/optic/magazine triple T-181.10 fixed, plus a no-loadout control); resource names are real vanilla GUIDs from the registry export, not invented. empty-warning-fields.json carries every empty the SCHEMA actually permits. Goldens are globbed (xtask/src/schema_gates.rs:1316) so both are auto-discovered — 4/4 PASS. Twelve negative-control mutants each failed with the exact expected message, proving the loadout fixture reaches the loadout $defs rather than passing vacuously. DISPROVED THE BRIEF'S PREMISE by measurement — see T-181.26 and T-181.31.

T-181.21.notes: ONE-LIFE integrity enforced @ dd79266d. Guard moved to DeployPlayerEx (the actual choke point) returning a new DENIED result, with AdminRespawn as the one documented opt-in bypass. The agent FALSIFIED the brief: death does NOT reach DoSpawn_S (that path is dead on a framework world since audit is swallowed) — it reaches SCR_RespawnComponent.NotifyReadyForSpawn_S, which invites a CLIENT spawn request and would have produced a fully VANILLA body. Closed by overriding CanRequestSpawn_S to refuse any request TBD_SpawnManager did not ticket (epoch-stamped, closed on spawn/kill/disconnect/5s timeout, fails closed). m_mDeadPlayers rekeyed to the durable PlayerBindKey — which required fixing a latent bug first: GetPlayerIdentityId returns a UUID and a NULL uuid formats to the same constant for everyone, so identity-keyed death tracking on the old string test would have made the first death kill the whole server. Also: departed dead players' seats retained (fixes round-never-ends when the last man rage-quits), AdminRespawn is now dead-until-proven-DEPLOYED, AssignSlotForPlayer got real exclusivity + a scanning round-robin. RetryDeploy race closed BY the choke-point guard rather than a duplicate check. UNVERIFIED, highest risk: the 5s possess-ticket window — if the request RPC lands outside it, deploys break outright. Needs a live run.

T-181.22.notes: ONE-LIFE hardened @ 1e301f89. Closed the possess route by modding SCR_PossessSpawnHandlerComponent's CanHandleRequest_S AND HandleRequest_S — calls vanilla routes through unconditionally, so the fix holds whether m_bIgnoreConditions is 0 or 1 (the packed value could not be read offline; it is now self-reported at runtime). Ticket made load-bearing: entity-keyed and consumed once, so a forged RplId matches nothing. Identity policy now matches its comment. adminOverride moved off the public signature so the compiler enforces the single bypass. NOT CLOSED, stated: one life is not durably enforceable on a listen/hosted server — engine limit.

T-181.23.notes: Parser gaps @ 94e72e3d. briefings/markers/zone label/ORBAT callsign+slot+kit all added, every field name verified against mission.schema.json rather than assumed. T-181.25.notes: OPERATOR RAN THE WORKBENCH PASS — AND IT FALSIFIED THE THEORY THE PASS EXISTED TO SATISFY. T-181.26.notes: Briefing wire sentinel. CONFIRMED THE v4 PREMISE FIRST, as asked: TBD_MissionLoader.LoadFromProfileFile opens $profile:missions/<id>.json and runs only TBD_MissionValidator — no JSON-schema validation on that path — and BeginLoad takes it directly whenever backendUrl/serverToken are empty, which is exactly what world-boot.sh writes. T-181.31 really did close /compiled. BUT IT ALSO MEASURED THE THING THE TICKET CALLED UNPROVABLE: string.Split KEEPS empty tokens on engine 1.7.0.54, so the pre-existing wire was ACCIDENTALLY correct and the defect was LATENT, not live — and it said so in the header and commit rather than overclaiming the fix. Adopted TBD_AdminData's BIJECTIVE FIELD_MARK over TBD_LobbyData's lossy '~': Unmark(Field(x))==x for every x, whereas '~' is a plausibility argument that loses a field authored as literally '~' — and the briefing carries the most free authored text of the three payloads. Checked before concluding that T-181.27's parallel-array pattern could NOT be generalised here: the record set needs ~8 variable-length arrays, Rpc caps at 8 params, orders already spend 3. FOUND TWO REAL BUGS INDEPENDENT OF THE SENTINEL, both of which bit under either split behaviour: m_sFactionKey was the one authored string reaching the wire UNSANITISED (a tab in a hand-staged slot.faction pushes the M record to six tokens, sails past the >=5 guard and renders the wrong two fields); and a rejected G record left `current` pointing at the PREVIOUS group, folding orphan R roles into another squad — misattribution being worse than omission on a briefing. SelfCheckWire round-trips a payload empty in every legal position, proven on a live boot with TWO NEGATIVE CONTROLS that both behaved (broken Unmark -> FAIL and world-boot escalated it; probe sample changed -> verdict read the real token count, not a constant). CORRECTED THE COMMAND CENTER'S VERIFICATION BAR: --mission= boots have zero players, so the briefing path never executes and 'use empty-warning-fields to exercise it' was false.

T-181.27.notes: Briefing ORDERS — situation/mission/execution per faction, the Arma-3 prose T-181.23 parsed and nothing read. Server BuildOrders splits each field into display paragraphs under a shared 6,000-byte budget, 16 paragraphs/field, WarnOnce so truncation is never silent nor spammy. Wire is THREE PARALLEL array<string> RPC params, deliberately NOT the existing tab/newline wire (T-181.19's precedent) — so an empty field cannot be confused with a missing one. Side discipline enforced at the wire: TBD_RpcAsk_Briefing() still takes NO ARGUMENTS so a client cannot phrase a cross-side request; faction comes from the server's own GetAssignedSlot; no slot returns before BuildOrders is reached, so the other side's prose is never in the client process at all. RUNTIME-VERIFIED via a /tmp harness executing the real functions against real parsed documents: 9/9 cross-side assertions on bridgehead (blufor and opfor author different orders at the same bridge), all three legal empty states on empty-warning-fields render ZERO paragraphs, hostile prose (leading/double/trailing newlines, tabs) handled, whitespace-only renders as absent, caps fire exactly, null RPC array does not crash. FOUND THREE THINGS THAT CORRECT THE DOCS: (1) string.Length() counts BYTES and Substring is byte-indexed — 'café latte'.Substring(0,4) returns broken UTF-8; hardened its own truncation to back off to a space and flagged the same exposure in TBD_MarkerService.CapLabel. (2) string.Trim() is NOT in the mutate-in-place family. (3) THE PROGRAM'S OWN PROBE ADVICE WAS WRONG — 'int n = s.Foo()' proves nothing because string->int coerces implicitly; the discriminating direction is 'string x = s.Foo()'. Both SLICE_WORKFLOW and the landmines are corrected. NOT VERIFIED: the rendering itself (TBD_UIBriefing cannot open until the Workbench rdb pass) and ORDERS_WRAP_WIDTH=64 is an estimate needing an operator retune. JIP explicitly left to T-181.28 with the reason: no new hole added, and the gap lives in another slice's file.

T-181.28.notes: Briefing JIP catch-up. Hooks vanilla's OWN one-shot latch: UpdateLocalPlayerController, which SCR_PlayerController.OnUpdate calls every frame while s_pLocalPlayerController is null and which then binds vanilla's local input listeners (vanilla_reference/SCR_PlayerController.c:532-556). So the waiting loop is the engine's — no timer added, the deleted 500 ms poll not reinstated, and it is as reliable as vanilla's own input binding because it IS that binding. Rejected OnOwnershipChanged with a cited reason: vanilla states at :111 that a listen server/SP client never calls it, which would have fixed dedicated clients and silently skipped a listen host — this program's recorded both-paths landmine in its original shape. ORDERS ride along STRUCTURALLY: the catch-up calls TBD_OnStageChanged, the screen re-requests on open, so there is one delivery path rather than two to keep in step. No seventh modded SCR_PlayerController block; invariants re-checked mechanically (6 blocks, 22 unique RPC names, no duplicate methods). jip:disabled deliberately does NOT gate the briefing, with a decisive reason: ReclaimDepartedSeat runs at TBD_SpawnManager.c:1613 BEFORE the JIP decision at :1616, so a reconnecting player is refused a BODY but KEEPS THEIR SEAT — they are on the roster and their squad is planning around them, and gating would blind exactly that player. FOUND THE ROOT CAUSE OF THE world-boot FLAKE: GetGame().GetWorkspace() is NON-NULL on a headless dedicated server, and TBD_LobbyStage.Start() uses it as a dedicated-server test. Proved it pre-existing by running the BASELINE at TBD_WORLDBOOT_SETTLE=12 (fails 3/3) vs default (passes 6/6). Fix handed to T-181.42, which owns UI/Lobby/**.

T-181.29.notes: Lobby picker stands down on the presence of a BODY, not only on the player's own deploy click. m_bInWorld resolved in BuildForPlayer from GetPlayerControlledEntity AHEAD of every early return and emitted ABOVE the X record — the 'roster unavailable' reply is precisely the one that would otherwise strand the picker over a live character. DID NOT FLIP m_bAutoDeploy, and found why that matters: Prefabs/Systems/TBD_GameMode.et declares TBD_SpawnManager with NO attribute override, so the [Attribute("1")] code default IS what ships — flipping is not 'changing a default someone might override', it takes effect on the next build, which makes it higher-stakes than the ticket framing implied and should be gated on an operator confirming a live client can deploy from the picker. Fix 1 is additive, also covers the JIP DeployJoiner and AdminRespawn paths which share the shape, and needed ZERO edits to TBD_SpawnManager.c. Deliberately does NOT latch: unlike m_bDeployed it is reassigned from each roster, so a wrong reading self-corrects and the worst case is a flicker rather than a picker gone for good. Negative control run in-session: renaming the D parse arm produced 'wire self-check FAIL lost=inWorld' -> WORLD BOOT: FAIL.

T-181.30.notes: Truth-in-comments + audit-ring hardening. 8 of 11 items FIXED, 2 reported (out of lane), 1 verified as already-handled. HIGHEST-LEVERAGE: the GetInstance() asymmetry, and the agent produced evidence rather than confidence — not 32 call sites in 16 files as filed but 40 in 19 (11 framework, 29 spawn), enumerated with enclosing functions, and ZERO are constructors or OnPostInit (earliest is TickLoading, itself a CallLater from OnPostInit). Runtime proof is PrintComponentRollCall, which runs strictly earlier, already resolves these classes via FindComponent, and is asserted by world-boot. Both statics DELETED, not left unread. EnsureConnectEpoch fixed: it minted a non-zero epoch for any id so IsSameConnection answered TRUE for a departed player — the exact opposite of the invariant stated three lines above it; now mints only when a controller exists, which is fail-closed at all 6 call sites and closes the leak. Duplicate-audit swallow fixed with m_mAuditedKey having exactly one writer. HasHost was KEPT — the finding was half right (TBD_SpawnManager never calls it, but Reconcile does), so the comment was corrected instead of deleting live code. Also found the TBD_SpectatorHost damage-manager refusal tests DamageManagerComponent while safestart only touches SCR_CharacterDamageManagerComponent, so the safestart framing never matched the guard at all. BONUS, from the full notes rather than the summary: NoteDeniedAccess de-duped per (player,surface), which bounds one client but not the population — ~6 surfaces x ~10 clients evicts the whole 60-entry ring, and s_mDeniedSeen's comment claimed an entry meant 'already took a ring slot', which stopped being true once the ring rolled it off, so refusals silently stopped reaching the trail on long-running servers. Now a hard 12-entry budget leaving 48 guaranteed for real actions. VERIFIED RATHER THAN ASSUMED on the coordinator's SelfCheckWire request: added the line, compiled, got 'Undefined function' cascading 12 errors because T-181.26 was unmerged at the time, reverted, and reported it as a dependency-ordering problem.

T-181.31.notes: /compiled is now schema-validated before it is served. get_compiled_mission serializes ONCE, validates those bytes, and serves THE SAME BYTES — so the checked value and the shipped value cannot drift. validate_mission_document went from zero production callers (only #[cfg(test)]) to gating the one route the mod consumes. PROVED THE GATE REJECTS SOMETHING REAL by short-circuiting it: 200 carrying "uid":"" (a minLength:1 violation) served straight to the game server; with the gate, 500 naming /slots/0/uid. THE FINDING THAT SHAPED THE SLICE: turning this on WOULD have broken working missions, because the mod and the schema disagree — blank role and groupCallsign are AddWarning in TBD_MissionValidator (mission loads) but minLength:1 violations in the schema, and a >120-char title is unchecked in the mod but maxLength:120 in the schema. All three are reachable because mission-editor-payload.schema.json deliberately leaves editor.slots[] unconstrained to keep write-side validation O(1) on 100k-slot missions, so the write-side gate cannot catch them. Rather than ship a gate that fires on inputs the generator routinely produces, the agent fixed the GENERATOR (map-engine-core/mission/flatten.rs) to substitute those three display values — with callsign falling back to the SQUAD ID not a literal, because a constant would collapse two unnamed squads onto one callsign and collide their derived slot ids, and a duplicate slot id IS a hard error in the mod. Blank uid deliberately NOT substituted: it is the durable identity the mod keys spawns, rosters and logs on, and inventing one is worse than refusing to serve. DECISIONS: 500 not 409, because the handler cannot distinguish bad stored data from a flatten bug and calling both 409 would let a compile regression hide as 'your mission is misconfigured'; findings returned deduped (the schema reaches slots[] twice so an undeduped count is exactly 2x wrong) and capped at 20 with the full count. COST MEASURED release-mode: 1k slots 6.9 ms, 10k 40 ms, 100k 410 ms, 367k 1.49 s on top of an existing 0.98 s flatten — ~1.4x an already-O(n) endpoint, once per mission load. Save-time validation CANNOT replace this: the document is a function of (version payload, mission row, flatten code, kit-alias table) and the last three change independently of a saved version. CAVEAT: TBD_MissionLoader.OnBackendFetchError discards the response body and fails over to its profile cache, so the mod never reads these findings — the tracing::error! line is the load-bearing diagnostic.

T-181.32.notes: ONE LIFE gate for hosts with no durable identity. SETTLED THE QUESTION THE SLICE HINGED ON: a correctly-configured dedicated server is in MODE 1 (real backend identity), HIGH confidence — vanilla's own SCR_PlayerIdentityUtils.c:35-38 hits Debug.Error('Dedicated server is not correctly configured to connect to the BI backend') when uid is empty AND session is Dedicated, i.e. VANILLA ITSELF classifies mode 3 on a dedicated box as a misconfiguration and names the fix. So refusing is cheap and does not brick real events. Practical discriminator: SCR_BaseGameMode.c:880-890 shows vanilla self-invokes the audit on Dedicated only when -config is ABSENT, and -config is what registers the backend room. RESIDUAL UNKNOWN, stated by the agent rather than hidden: BackendApi.GetPlayerIdentityId's engine-side contract is in NO oracle (BackendApi absent from all 7991 vanilla_api_classes.tsv entries and from Scripts/GameLib/generated/online/), so this is strong inference from vanilla SCRIPT's error text, not a measurement. Built: StageRefusalFor(stage) refusing SAFE_START/LIVE while any connected player resolves NUMERIC — a LIVE SCAN, deliberately not a session latch, because vanilla fires its audit at registration BEFORE identity exists so a healthy server emits one transient player:<id> per join; latching would have refused LIVE on a correctly-configured server, the exact opposite of intent. LOBBY/BRIEFING stay open so the operator can read the refusal. Admin waiver '#tbd identity override I-ACCEPT-NO-ONE-LIFE' (exact phrase as a separate argument, audited both ways, session-scoped, re-announces on every stage it passes). Latch now per KeyModeLabel — it also found the VERDICT SENTENCE was shared, so 'Expected on a local/listen host' was telling operators their broken event server was fine. ALSO FIXED the JsonLoadContext MAJOR in this file: HasAuthoredLoadout tests content, so bridgehead went from '18 with a JSON loadout, 0 kit-only' + 36 spurious gear=0/0 lines to '0 with, 18 kit-only' + 0 lines. CORRECTED FOUR DOC ERRORS: mode 3 is NOT 'local PIE' (PIE is not Dedicated so vanilla synthesizes a name hash — PIE is mode 2, and the old comment would have led an operator to dismiss a real misconfiguration); the vanilla excerpt omitted both early returns (playerId<=0, !Replication.IsServer()) which are real mode-3 sources — the latter is why IdentityRefusalFor now has a client guard; identity is valid ONLY after OnPlayerAuditSuccess (undocumented timing precondition); citation drift :33 -> :31. NEEDS A ONE-LINER in TBD_FrameworkManager.SetStage — handed to the T-181.38 agent, which owns that file. NOT VERIFIABLE ON THIS LANE: the gate's FIRING path — world-boot has zero players so PlayerBindKey is never called and modes 1/2/3 are structurally untestable; only the not-firing path is proven. Agent also edited TBD_AdminService.c + TBD_AdminCommands.c to make the override reachable (both Gamemode/, disjoint from live agents) and flagged it.

T-181.33.notes: Safestart now SAVES AND RESTORES each body's prior damage-handling value instead of forcing true. m_mHeld became map<IEntity, ref TBD_SafestartHold> carrying the arm generation PLUS the value safestart found, read once in ApplyTo before that body's first mutation and never re-read. THE GETTER EXISTS — IsDamageHandlingEnabled(), so the prompt's 'least-bad fallback' was unnecessary; corroborated in shipped vanilla by two sites that READ it without ever setting it (SCR_DamageDisabledTooltipDetail.c:20, SCR_HealthTooltipDetail.c:21), i.e. a general-purpose state query not a set-then-confirm idiom. KEY DESIGN CALL: EnableDamageHandling(false) stays unconditional and never consults the getter — the naive fix would trade 'forces damage on' for 'a getter that lies leaves EVERYONE invulnerable', which is strictly worse and is the exact disaster this file exists to prevent. Only the hand-back depends on the read. Leaving a body off because that is how we found it is counted and loud (leftDisabled= on the lift line, a WARNING, and StatusLine()), with a foundAlreadyOff= warning at ARM minutes earlier. Absent record means 'was enabled', assigned explicitly at both construction sites rather than resting on a field initializer, because whether Enforce applies one to a new-ed plain class is a runtime property no probe can observe and the failure direction is catastrophic. Idempotence is structural: success and left-disabled both drop from the map, a failure re-inserts THE SAME hold object, and Arm() deliberately does not clear m_mHeld because clearing would cement safestart's own handiwork as the body's 'prior' state. EVERY behavioural claim is compile-verified only — the agent CONFIRMED rather than assumed this by re-running the mission boot and grepping: the stage machine reaches LOADING->LOBBY and stops because zero players means it never advances to SAFE_START, so Arm/SweepApply/ApplyTo/Restore/RestoreOne never executed.

T-181.34.notes: Cargo container enum + the kit-alias GATE. $defs/cargoContainer = [vest,pants,jacket,backpack] added to BOTH mission.schema.json and loadout-export.schema.json (which carried the same cargo rows with the same bare string). The reasoning that makes an enum correct HERE and wrong for kit: this vocabulary is closed by the ENGINE's worn-garment areas, not by content, so it can never fight a registry. KIT DECISION — A GATE, NOT AN ENUM, and the agent was right to refuse the enum: kit aliases come from Data/registry.json which is generated and extensible (kit-aliases.json literally carries 'generatedFrom'), so a closed enum would need re-cutting on every content addition, would go stale silently, and would reject valid missions authored against a newer registry. Schema keeps checking SHAPE (^kit:[a-z0-9_]+$); EXISTENCE is a registry question, so it moved into a gate that reads the same file the game server reads — TBD_MissionValidator.CheckSlotKit's runtime check, relocated to where it costs 2 s instead of a rejected server. The gate walks slots[].kit AND orbat[].groups[].roles[].kit (the flatten turns the latter into the former, so checking only slots lets a dangling alias hide in a 1.0 document) and pins kit-aliases.json to the registry so the pair cannot drift — a one-sided addition there does not error, it makes the flatten silently compile an authored medic into a rifleman. New packages/tbd-schema/golden-missions-invalid/ holds fixtures the gate MUST reject, each declaring the JSON pointer it must be rejected AT so a fixture failing for an unrelated typo is a false green. PROVED BY MUTATION: deleting the enum makes the typo fixture accepted (gate reports the check is gone); removing kit:us_medic reproduces T-181.36 in seconds and names both the slot AND the orbat role the runtime validator never looks at; adding a bogus alias to the registry only trips the mirror check. preset: is REPORTED not failed, because nothing in the mod resolves a preset alias today and failing would enforce a rule the runtime does not have.

T-181.35.notes: In-game identity linking — and THE FIRST END-TO-END PROOF AGAINST THE REAL BACKEND in this program. The agent found the dev stack already live (Axum on :8080, db on 5434) and refused to settle for a mirror: POST /me/link on the real backend minted code 457879; the MOD posted to the real /ingest/link-confirm and got the real handler's body back ({linked:true,discord_id:...}); users.arma_id was written, identity_link_codes.consumed_at set, an audit_logs identity.link row created; replaying the code returned the real 404; the exact join telemetry.rs:238 runs now returns a discord_id instead of zero rows; and a match-results POST in the byte shape TBD_ResultsReporter emits populated match_player_stats.discord_id (previously NULL) and moved users.total_deployments 0 -> 1, proving the stat recompute ran. ONE HONEST GAP NAMED RATHER THAN GLOSSED: the attendance UPDATE additionally needs a non-empty event_id resolving to a registration, and the proof payload had event_id:'' — so the resolved list going non-empty was observed (which is what everything hangs off and what was broken) but not that final UPDATE. Dev DB restored to exactly as found. REFUSES to link an empty or synthetic (00bbbddd- name hash) identity, because users.arma_id is UNIQUE so a seat lease or name hash is a PERMANENT mis-binding, not a recoverable mistake. Branches on RestCallback.GetHttpCode(), never on response text — six distinct outcomes plus a watchdog. Serial bounded queue because RestCallbackFunc carries no user data, so a response cannot otherwise be correlated to a player, plus a recycled-player-id guard on async replies. Caught a real bug in its own code via a probe control: it had written `code.Trim();` as a bare statement, which does nothing. KNOWN LIMIT, not fixable from script: the code is typed in PUBLIC chat and OnNewMessage is the receive-side display hook, so consuming it suppresses nothing — on success the backend consumes the code in the same transaction, and every failure reply tells the player to generate a new one. Real fix is a UI field, blocked on the rdb pass. Declined to add a second modded SCR_ChatComponent, since both blocks would override OnNewMessage and the downside is silently killing the shipped admin surface.

T-181.36.notes: Fixed by adding kit:us_medic to Data/registry.json (+ mirrored to kit-aliases.json) rather than editing the fixture, because a US medic is ALREADY a real thing this project ships — seeded at api/seeds/registry_dev.sql:20 and served by GET /api/v1/registry. The prefab GUID was MEASURED not invented: {C9E4FEAF5AAC8D8C}Character_US_Medic.et agrees across the T-068.10.2 Workbench census, registry-items.workbench.json and the API seed. Inventing a GUID would have been strictly worse than the bug — the validator would pass and the spawn would fail. slot-loadout-coverage now boots PASS (errors=0, warnings=2 at baseline, 4/4 repeats); bridgehead stays PASS at 18. LATENT SECOND INSTANCE FOUND: last-stand-at-montfort.json carries four dangling kit:uk_* aliases. Reforger vanilla ships no UK faction so they cannot be added honestly — waived with that reason in KNOWN_UNRESOLVABLE_KITS. They are ORBAT-only today and go live the moment that mission is flattened to slots.

T-181.37.notes: Per-trigger reachability checks in the validator. CORRECTED THE COMMAND CENTER'S BRIEF TWICE. (1) empty-warning-fields does NOT have 'no zones at all' — it has three including a real objective_capture, so its all_objectives_captured is SATISFIED; what it actually fails is time_limit with 'flow': {} . The brief had that mission's two triggers exactly backwards, and that inversion is the entire baseline movement. (2) THE LOAD-BEARING FINDING: every runtime warning the brief credited is INVISIBLE TO EVERY GATE. ArmRoundClock's two warnings hang off OnEnterLive, and world-boot never leaves LOADING with zero players; ReportTriggerCoverage counts objectives usable at BUILD, measured on a live montfort boot as 'built objectives=2 usable=2 capture=0 destroy=1 hold=1' — so it emits NO objective_destroyed warning, because the INERT verdict comes from ArmDestroyTargets at first LIVE evaluation, which never runs. Montfort's known-dead destroy trigger has never been observed by any gate. 'Already warns' was true of the code and false of the gate — which is what made a validator-side check worth building rather than redundant. ERROR-vs-WARNING rule, now in the class header: ERROR when the mission cannot be PLAYED, WARNING when it can be played but not ENDED — because an ERROR parks the server in LOADING, a worse outage than a round that runs long and gets ended by an admin. All five reachability findings are WARNINGs; the pre-existing faction_eliminated ERROR was KEPT because fewer than two sides with slots is not a round that ends late, it is not a PvP event. AVOIDED THE SECOND COPY by deleting three constants outright and reading TBD_ObjectiveRegistry.TRIGGER_*/TYPE_*/KindOf() and TBD_MissionFlow.ResolveSeconds() instead. Deliberately did NOT restate montfort's destroy-target gap in the validator, because hardcoding 'this build does not place entities[]' would bake a fact that becomes false the day an entity-placement slice lands — the exact drift this slice exists to catch. Proved with six fixtures in one batch including control D (everything satisfied, warnings=0) — D not firing is what makes the other five mean anything. Baseline msn_0e77ab 2 -> 3, with a header note to tighten back when the fixture is fixed.

T-181.38.notes: The mission `flow` block is parsed and honoured. ABSENT sentinel (-1000000) distinguishes an unauthored field from an authored 0, which matters because timeLimitSeconds:0 is a real statement ('no limit'). ResolveSeconds returns authored/default/INVALID (negative is illegal under the schema and is reported at ERROR, never clamped). PROVED BY READ-BACK, not by claim: the safestart line quotes TBD_SafestartManager.StatusLine()'s own m_iConfiguredSeconds, and three goldens produced three DISTINCT clocks (5:00 / 3:00 / 2:00) where the old hardcoded 300 had matched bridgehead by coincidence. Round clock proven at runtime with TWO NEGATIVE CONTROLS: duration without trigger, and trigger without duration, both correctly refusing to arm. Also fixed OnEnterLive returning early without faction_eliminated, which is why empty-warning-fields entered LIVE with nothing watching it. JIP REVERSES PART OF T-181.15, deliberately and stated: always/absent = today's behaviour byte-for-byte, until_safestart_end shuts at LIVE, disabled = LOBBY only (the third rung is a judgement call — BRIEFING is where a side plans around a fixed roster). last-stand-at-montfort authors disabled, so a reconnect after BRIEFING there now gets no body; they still connect, nobody is kicked. Placed T-181.32's SetStage hook itself. safeStartSeconds needed ZERO lines in TBD_SafestartManager — used the existing AdminSetSeconds seam.

T-181.39.notes: Objectives — all three types, server-authoritative, built ON TOP of T-181.18's zones with NO geometry of its own (containment is TBD_Zone.Contains everywhere). Reads its rules via a SECOND JsonLoadContext pass over GetRawJson(), because TBD_MissionZoneRulesStruct is structurally blind to captureSeconds/contestable/holdSeconds/targetAlias/points and Backend/** was another agent's lane; joins by index with id verification, seam to consolidate is one function. SIX DESIGN DECISIONS with no prior art, each justified in-code and each JSON-overridable — notably progress HOLDS when uncontested-but-empty (under one life, decay favours the side with more bodies and punishes casualties permanently) and taking an enemy-held objective is TWO-STAGE (neutralise then capture) so holding ground is worth something. Missing rules treated ASYMMETRICALLY on purpose: absent captureSeconds defaults to 120s loudly (an inert capture objective takes all_objectives_captured with it and the round silently runs to the time limit), but absent holdSeconds goes INERT with a diagnostic (no defensible default for a whole-round timer — guessing ends the event at the wrong moment). Destruction signal is vanilla's own: DamageManagerComponent.GetState() != EDamageState.DESTROYED, cited at SpectateTargetComponent.c:26. RUNTIME-PROVEN that the second pass populates: capture=120, contestable=1, hold=2700, targetAlias are values the loader's struct CANNOT SEE, and bounds match the golden's circle exactly. DELIBERATELY LEFT OUT, each with a reason: no objective RPC (no consumer can exist while .layout is rdb-gated, and it would add to the unsettled 6x modded SCR_PlayerController risk) — the seam BuildBoardForPlayer resolves the viewer's side server-side so there is no faction parameter to forge; objective_destroy CANNOT COMPLETE on today's build and it refused to fake it (the signal is real, the TARGET does not exist — entities[] is unmodelled and comp:ammo_cache is not in the registry) so it arms, finds nothing, goes inert and says why; points parsed and exposed but not scored, because winConditions.mode 'points_then_attrition' implies a scoring system that does not exist. NONE OF THE BEHAVIOUR HAS EVER RUN — zero players means no presence sample, no capture, no contest, no hold clock, no end trigger, not once.

T-181.40.notes: Radio plan from radioPlan.nets[] — and it OVERTURNED THE BRIEF'S PREMISE. The brief expected 'VOIP is probably not reachable from script'. It is: the whole chain is proto external and compile-proved with a failing negative control — SCR_GadgetManagerComponent.GetGadgetManager -> GetGadgetsByType(EGadgetType.RADIO|RADIO_BACKPACK) -> SCR_RadioComponent.GetRadioComponent() -> BaseRadioComponent.GetTransceiver(i) -> BaseTransceiver.SetFrequency(kHz). No CVON, no partner mod. THE BLOCKER IS A WORLD ASSET: the engine warns every boot 'World doesn't contain RadioManagerEntity to support any BaseRadioComponent', and worlds/TBD_Dev_POC.ent is a 62-byte bare SubScene placing nothing. Confirmed independently from script via ChimeraWorld.GetRadioManager(). Same class as the stale rdb gating the menu presets — one Workbench pass settles it and tuning then works with NO code change, because TBD_RadioTuner only counts a net as tuned after READING THE FREQUENCY BACK off the same transceiver. Until then it honestly says tuning is unavailable. Refused to spawn a RadioManagerEntity from script despite it compiling, because the world's BaseRadioComponents are created during Game::LoadEntities before any script runs, so adoption is unprovable headless — shipping it would have been a plausible-looking thing that might do nothing. Parse is RUNTIME-proven on three goldens (4/4/3 nets) plus a mangled copy giving 1 accepted / 3 rejected with distinct reasons.

T-181.41.notes: Worn-kit audit re-homed onto the kit-only path, and the deadline VERIFIED rather than inherited. The resumed agent did not take its predecessor's 'from measurement, not feel' claim on trust — it reproduced the measurement with a temporary probe plus a failing control in the same run, then reverted both and confirmed byte-identical files by md5. The claim HOLDS (kit clothing is synchronous: 17 slots settled on attempt 1 at 250 ms; the control, pointing kit:us_sl at a base character prefab, produced exactly one NAKED ERROR and failed the gate) — but the UPPER BOUND WAS UNDERSTATED. Measured on two independent boots: bodies materialise +2.947/+2.983 s after the line the harness polls for, and 'Game destroyed' lands +2.985/+2.968 s after that. The predecessor wrote that a 3 s deadline 'raced' the kill; it does not race, it LOSES BY 32 ms. The shipped 1 s deadline leaves 1.97 s of margin, and that margin IS TBD_WORLDBOOT_SETTLE — now said out loud in-code. Two structural checks back the design: grep for Callqueue().Remove across the mod (20 hits, none in either touched file) proves the T-181.15 by-function cancel hazard cannot reach the audit ticks; and SpawnEntityPrefab appears exactly once in TBD_SpawnManager, inside SpawnSlotBody, which has two call sites — so coverage is total with no second body path. CORRECTED A PREMISE IN ITS OWN BRIEF: 'world-boot has zero players so the audit never executes there' is FALSE for --mission= mode, because the slot lineup materialises at MISSION START not on join. Recorded one lifetime caveat rather than fixing it on speculation: CallLater holds no reference, so Cancel -> m_bDone -> PruneDoneLoadoutApps can drop the last strong ref with a tick queued. That shape predates this slice, is shared with VerifyTick, and this slice moves exposure DOWN (250 ms vs up to 3 s); reaching it needs a live client, so it is labelled unproven and the note warns that lengthening AUDIT_TICK_MS widens it.

T-181.42.notes: Lobby wire: bijective marker + BOOT-armed self-check + two real bug fixes + the gate flake. SAID PLAINLY THAT THE RENAME ALONE WOULD HAVE BEEN COSMETIC: no committed golden contains a '~', and it independently re-measured split-empties=kept, so the lobby's empty-field handling was already correct and the '~' loss is a latent authoring hazard only. What earns the slice is the other four. FOUND A BUG REACHABLE FROM AUTHORED JSON THE SCHEMA PERMITS: TBD_SpawnManager.BuildSlotRoster formatted slot.Key()/faction/groupCallsign/role into a TSV with NO sanitisation, and mission.schema.json has minLength:1 but NO pattern on any of them — a callsign authored 'AL<TAB>PHA' produced a seven-field row that sailed past the consumer's '<6' guard and shifted every column, so role rendered as 'PHA', the real role was read as the STATE (seat matches neither OPEN nor DEAD, therefore unselectable) and holderId came from 'OPEN'.ToInt() = 0. It hardened the lobby parser to exact arity and reported upstream rather than editing another lane; the command center then fixed it at the source in BuildSlotRoster. Also fixed the same rejected-record cursor bug T-181.26 found in the briefing, gated by a control. FIXED THE world-boot FLAKE, and put the guard in Raise() NOT Start() with a reason: Start() is a one-shot at +2000 ms so gating it on a controller that may not be up yet would mean the picker silently never appears, whereas Tick polls every 500 ms so gating the raise is self-healing. 3/3 FAIL at SETTLE=12 before, 3/3 PASS after. THREE CONTROLS ALL FAILED AS REQUIRED, including one that isolates the cursor fix alone (phase 1 clean, orphanShape lost). OPS CAVEAT WORTH KEEPING: its first control run reported the UNPATCHED verdict — the patch was not live at boot despite a clean compile — so it re-ran verifying the patch present immediately before AND after the boot. A stale-patch run looks exactly like a vacuous check.

T-181.43.notes: wireSafeString pattern ^[^\x00-\x1F\x7F]$ (C0 controls + DEL), shared $def, $ref'd from 10 authored fields. WENT BEYOND THE BRIEF IN THE RIGHT DIRECTION: it constrained group.callsign and role.slot as well, because flatten.rs:518 copies those VERBATIM into slot.groupCallsign/slot.role and interpolates them into slot.id with no re-validation — so constraining only the slot fields would have forbidden the symptom while permitting the cause. Chose the control block over a bare tab/CR/LF blocklist for three reasons it verified rather than asserted: it costs authoring nothing (all four goldens scanned, zero control characters; Alpha-1/2, Saint-Pierre Depot, Cafe, blufor:Alpha:RFL:0 all pass), it is a CLOSED class that cannot drift, and it covers siblings nothing strips today — RosterField and Sanitise each replace exactly \t\n\r, so NUL (a terminator where string.Length() counts BYTES) and VT/FF were undefended. DELIBERATELY DID NOT BAN, each checked in source: '.' (TBD_BriefingData.FIELD_MARK is a bijective per-field PREFIX, so an authored dot cannot confuse a reader), '~' (the RETIRED lossy TBD_LobbyData sentinel — forbidding it would enshrine an abandoned convention), ':' (load-bearing inside slot.id), and the zero-width/bidi class (a display-SPOOFING hazard, not a wire-FRAMING one; folding two defects behind one pattern means a failure stops naming its cause). EXCLUDED briefing.situation/mission/execution with a good reason: they do not ride a delimited wire at all — TBD_BriefingService ships them as parallel array<string> RPC params precisely to preserve paragraph breaks — so a NEWLINE THERE IS LEGITIMATE AUTHORING and constraining it would have broken real missions. TWO must-fail fixtures, not one, because ten $ref sites behind one $def means a single fixture leaves nine free to lose the constraint unnoticed; proven not-false-green by stripping only the pattern line and watching both flip to 'ACCEPTED it — the check this fixture pins is gone'. Two throwaway probes settled silent-loosening risks rather than assuming: minLength:1 as a SIBLING of $ref still applies under 2020-12, and '$' is strict end-of-haystack here (not the PCRE trailing-newline variant). BEHAVIOUR CHANGE THE OPERATOR SHOULD KNOW: /compiled is validated at runtime, so a STORED mission carrying a control character in one of the ten fields now answers 500, and TBD_MissionLoader.OnBackendFetchError discards the body and fails over to its cached copy — the symptom is 'the server is still running the previous mission' with the cause only in the API log. Same shape as T-181.34's enum, and better than a corrupted roster, but real.

T-181.44.notes: Save-time control-char scan + surfacing /compiled rejections. BOTH HALVES, argued: they serve disjoint humans and disjoint failure sets — the mod path is the only place the 500 body reaches the game host and covers rejections the author could never anticipate (a flatten regression, a dangling kit alias, the live faction_eliminated rejection), while the Creator path covers the one class the author can fix, at the moment they can fix it. O(1) CONSTRAINT RESPECTED AND MEASURED: the rule lives in code not the schema, because the schema form costs a per-item object walk plus a regex per slot; instead a single linear pass over the already-parsed serde_json::Value, byte-scanning two short strings per slot (every UTF-8 continuation byte is >= 0x80, so byte scan == char scan over C0+DEL). At 367k slots / 65.7 MB: parse 615.6 ms, scan 34.5 ms = 5.6% of a parse that has to happen anyway. Body capped at 900 B because Print() DISCARDS a line over 1024 B rather than truncating — an uncapped body would log nothing, which is the very failure being fixed. THE LOAD-BEARING TEST is save_scan_agrees_with_the_compiled_schema: it runs the REAL compiler against the REAL schema over a matrix of authored defects and asserts the save-time scan fires exactly when the compiled document would be rejected, both directions, with anti-vacuity guards (>=4 cases must reach the schema pattern, >=2 must compile clean) so an A==B over cases that never fire cannot pass. Integration test proven failing on base: 201 CREATED with a tab stored in the callsign.

T-181.45.notes: 10 .meta sidecars for the input .conf files. CONFResourceClass is not a guess — enumerated every *ResourceClass string in the server binary; there is no Action/ActionContext-specific class. RETIRED A RECORDED LANDMINE: '.meta is only honoured after Workbench rewrites the rdb' is FALSE. Proved with two probes on a loose addon — repointed a .meta to a GUID present nowhere in the rdb and the world still loaded by that GUID, then pointed scenarioId at one of the NEW GUIDs and the engine echoed the path back and reached class inspection, which it could only do from a GUID->path mapping the new sidecar supplied. So the engine scans and reads .meta at startup; no operator pass needed. ALSO ESTABLISHED registration alone IS enough here, unlike the menu presets: vanilla's gproj names only three Configs/System resources (two single-valued InputManagerSettings fields a mod cannot append to, plus the MenuConfigs list), and its own 26 ActionContext confs and all Actions confs appear nowhere in it — the directory is the contract. Data/*.json correctly left alone, TESTED not assumed: added a JSONResourceClass sidecar for registry.json and reproduced the identical failure, because TBD_Registry.Load uses FileIO.FileExists on a $TBD_Framework: alias — a filesystem call, not a resource lookup, so GUID identity is irrelevant to it.

T-181.46.notes: NOT AUTHORING — A COMPILER BUG. The operator asked to drop faction_eliminated from their mission and it turned out not to be theirs to drop: winConditions is SYNTHESIZED in flatten.rs, which documents at :430 that the editor never authors it, and end_on was the hardcoded literal ['time_limit','faction_eliminated'] for EVERY mission. So every single-faction mission was unloadable — TBD_MissionValidator rejects the document, the server parks in LOADING, and the author has no field to edit. Fixed by declaring faction_eliminated only when at least two factions actually HOLD SLOTS, counted over the flattened slots rather than factions[] because a faction can be declared with zero seats, which is exactly the shape that surfaced it. Regression test proven to FAIL without the change ('one-sided mission must not declare faction_eliminated: [time_limit, faction_eliminated]') and pass with it; 38/38 lib tests green. THE NEGATIVE CONTROL EARNED ITS KEEP TWICE: (1) `cargo build -p map-engine-core` compiles NOTHING in src/mission/** because the module is behind #[cfg(feature = "mission")] which is off by default — a deliberate syntax error built clean in 0.07s and exit 0, so the first version of this fix was entirely unverified and would have shipped that way. The real build is `--features mission`, or just build website-api. (2) With the feature on, the build immediately caught a borrow error the eye had missed: `slots: doc_slots` moves the vec before win_conditions could read it, so the count had to move above the struct literal. RELATED, STILL OPEN: `flow` is hardcoded in the same place (briefingSeconds 600, safeStartSeconds 300, timeLimitSeconds 5400, jip until_safestart_end) — which is why every golden carries those exact numbers, and why T-181.38 parses values no author can currently set.

T-181.47.notes: Rebuilt the UI layout foundation on the idiom shipped layouts actually use. ROOT CAUSE WAS ONE EMPTY BLOCK: TBD_ListRow.layout had `Slot ButtonWidgetSlot { }` with no HorizontalAlign, and a child with no align keeps its DESIRED size — which for the FrameWidgetClass inside it is ZERO. So every row collapsed to a sliver, and with no `Wrap 0` the text wrapped one character per line: the vertical column the operator saw. Same defect class 6x in the shell, where four button Body/Background/Label widgets had NO Slot block at all. HorizontalAlign 3 = Stretch CONFIRMED from vanilla_reference/Scripts/Core/generated/UI/LayoutHorizontalAlign.c rather than inferred from CRF frequency. Row body is now SizeLayout > Overlay > (Background, Accent, HorizontalLayout) because Overlay is the stacking primitive and stretches while a Frame has no intrinsic size; Title/Detail ride LayoutSlot { SizeMode Fill FillWeight 1 }. CORRECTED THE COMMAND CENTER'S ORACLE: the brief said Anchor/SizeX/SizeY are absent from the engine string table and therefore invalid — but with controls, ImageWidgetClass, TextWidgetClass, HorizontalAlign, Padding and HeightOverride ALL miss too and are all valid, so a miss is evidence of nothing; and the first probe returned a SILENT all-miss because `strings` is absent in the container with stderr suppressed. Anchor IS honoured, proven by PrimaryAction (Anchor 1 1 1 1, OffsetLeft -288) rendering bottom-right on the operator's screen. Built scripts/mod/verify-ui-layouts.sh (brace balance, slot-class whitelist, geometry invariant, container children missing a slot or an align, and the FindAnyWidget name contract) — and its FIRST CUT PASSED THE KNOWN-BROKEN FILES because GUID strings desynced the brace counter; fixed, it lands C6 on TBD_ListRow.layout:13, the exact empty slot block, and rejects five injected defects one per arm. Now gate step 6 of 12. Widget-name contract preserved with zero renames, 16 names. ADMITTED GUESSES, each with blast radius: `Size 3 44` for the accent rail, AlignableSlot for SizeLayout/ScrollLayout children (their specific slot classes exist in the generated API but appear in NO shipped layout), the 2px row-gap padding, and FocusAnchor deliberately not added.

T-181.48.notes: The picker and the auto-deploy wave cannot both be on. m_bAutoDeploy shipped as 1 and TBD_GameMode.et never overrode it, so the dev wave seated everyone ~250ms into LOBBY; T-181.29's ShouldStandDown() then closed the picker ~500ms after it opened. Operator saw no UI and no reason. TBD_GameMode.et now overrides to 0 (code default stays 1 for a bare prefab) and OnStageChanged names the live route into the world on every LOBBY entry. Confirmed in the operator's 20:39 session: action=PICKER-auto-deploy-off. Necessary but NOT sufficient - the picker still does not raise (T-181.49).

T-181.49.notes: Make the lobby raise path survivable and observable. MEASURED: TBD_GameMode is constructed TWICE per Workbench session (World Editor 20:39:34, Play 20:39:59) while all TBD_LobbyStage state is static and survives between them. TBD_LobbyStage.Start is a one-shot CallLater(...,false) behind three guards that log NOTHING, and it fires ~200ms BEFORE the framework manager is ready (Start ~20:40:01.32 vs roll-call 20:40:01.523) - losing that race is permanent and silent. Nine of eleven guards on the path emit no log at all. Also: TBD_MenuStack.Reset()/CloseAll() have ZERO callers, so a stale weak entry makes Raise()'s IsOpen check true forever. Fix: self-healing retry arm, statics reset on arm not only teardown, wire up MenuStack.Reset, log every guard, and replace the GetWorkspace() authority test with RplSession.Mode()==RplMode.Dedicated (neither oracle ever used GetWorkspace for this).

T-181.50.notes: Pre-slot body + kill the vanilla loading placeholder. Vanilla SCR_RespawnSystemComponent.OnInit:270 builds a loading splash DIRECTLY on the workspace (above menu-manager menus) and mutes SFX; it is destroyed ONLY from the vanilla spawn pipeline, which we bypass and actively block in CanRequestSpawn_S. Our modded class overrides OnPlayerRegistered_S/OnPlayerAuditSuccess_S/CanRequestSpawn_S but NOT OnInit, so nothing ever tears it down. Second and larger half: with auto-deploy off the player has NO controlled entity, therefore no camera, therefore nothing to render behind the picker - every session where the picker was visible had a body. Adopt PlayableSelector's ghost pattern (invisible AI-less character in a per-player cell far off map, SetInitialMainEntity, deleted on slot commit) plus a spectator camera.

T-181.51.notes: Two backend calls share ONE root cause, not two URL typos. ServiceAuth (middleware/auth.rs:108) reads only x-service-token; TBD_MissionListLoader:99 and TBD_RosterLoader:127 both send 'Authorization, Bearer' while the three loaders that work all send X-Service-Token. Fixing only the URLs turns 404 into 401. list_missions is owner-scoped (push_filters ... me) so ServiceAuth cannot be bolted onto it, and NO roster route has ever existed (full-crate grep). Add GET /api/v1/ingest/missions and GET /api/v1/ingest/events/{id}/roster, both ServiceAuth, mirroring the /ingest/link-confirm pattern; repoint both mod loaders and fix their stale @route comments.

T-181.52.notes: Log-noise demotion + oracle lane gap. Demote the magazine first-attempt 'mount refused' line from WARNING to INFO (the deterministic-swap design intends it; it reads as a fault). Document cargo:backpack DEGRADED as a mission/kit authoring mismatch, not a mod bug. Separately: scripts/mod/slice-worktree.sh links only crf_framework and vanilla_reference, so slice agents have NO PlayableSelector oracle - it sits outside the repo at ~/Projects/Archive/Reforger_Lobby/PlayableSelector-main. T-181.50 copies its design, so the lane must be linked (design-mirror ONLY - no licence, never copy code).

T-181.53.notes: Delete the pre-slot ghost; keep the pre-slot camera. OPERATOR-CONFIRMED LIVE 2026-07-25 20:5x: the ghost never worked - CELL_ALTITUDE_M=100000 (taken from PlayableSelector) is outside Everon's world bounds, so the engine raised a MODAL 'Entity out of world bounds' assertion at TBD_PreSlotBody.c:669 SpawnGhostEntity AND refused the control transfer ('the engine did not transfer control to the ghost - rolled back'). The session then ran end to end anyway: camera UP, picker OPEN, claim, DEPLOY, groundDelta=0.011. So the ghost's value was defensive and unproven while its cost was a modal dialog mid-mission, which would be fatal in a live event. T-181.50's own header already called the ghost 'the smaller half' and the camera 'the actual black screen' fix - the live run confirmed it. Keep: TBD_PreSlotCamera.c and the vanilla loading-placeholder teardown (both confirmed working in the same log).

T-181.54.notes: Correct a mission-loader warning that told the operator a falsehood, and add scripts/mod/test-mission.sh. OPERATOR-REPORTED LIVE: staging a golden produced 'RUNNING A CACHED MISSION - this is the last document the backend served successfully, NOT THE ONE CONFIGURED'. That last clause can NEVER be true: LoadFromProfileFile reads $profile:missions/<missionId>.json, so the file is KEYED BY the configured id and the mission identity always matches. What can differ is the VERSION. Worse, it labelled a deliberate stage as a fault. MEASURED discriminator against the live API: a golden's msn_* id returns 400 {invalid id} because the API validates the id SHAPE before lookup, while a valid-but-absent uuid returns 404 {mission not found} - so 400 means this id was never a backend mission and the disk file is intended, not stale. Loader now threads the http code into TryProfileFallbackAfterRestFailure and branches: 400 -> event-level 'staged on disk' note (plus the no-schema-validation caveat), anything else -> the stale-VERSION warning. NOT VERIFIABLE BY THE GATE: world-boot --mission= forces backendUrl='' so it never takes the REST error path; the branch is confirmed on the operator's next live reload.

tickets.user_story: As an event host I load a TBD mission from JSON, players slot in a TBD-styled lobby, read the briefing, deploy into their JSON-defined body and loadout, live one life, and the round resolves on a JSON-defined win condition.
acceptance: make mod-compile exits 0 on clean source and non-zero with file:line on a broken .c, with no Workbench
make verify-capability reports zero UNTRIAGED CRF capabilities
enf lookup resolves a real symbol to file:line and returns NOT FOUND for an invented one
A player joins, slots, reads the briefing, deploys with the JSON loadout, dies once terminally, and an admin can respawn them
A JSON-defined win condition ends the round

tickets.summary: Arsenal silently drops three of four weapon slots at compile. mod_slot_loadout (crates/map-engine-core/src/mission/flatten.rs:397-410) reads only slotIndex==0 && slotType=="primary". tickets.summary: CANCELLED — premise fixed by T-181.46 (c4fabcb2, 2026-07-25 19:09), 43 minutes after this ticket was filed. flatten.rs:617-635 now derives endOn from flattened slots and only emits faction_eliminated when >=2 factions actually hold slots, which is exactly the zero-slot-stub case described here.

tickets.title: A transient Discord failure demotes an admin to enlisted
tickets.summary: oauth.rs:83-90 collapses an error and an empty result into one empty vec; sync_roles then deletes all user_discord_roles rows, resolves Enlisted and persists it. A timeout during login destroys the snapshot so resync_all_roles cannot restore it. This is the script that prepares a server profile for testing missions.
